Ion Source.caption: Ion Source tab, box birth distribution (the default): ions are placed uniformly inside a rectangular volume whose extents are the box dx/dy/dz fields.
Ion Source tab, point birth distribution: zero declared extent, so downstream spread is set entirely by the optics (the app prints the L-216 advisory for exactly this case).
Ion Source tab, disc birth distribution: a filled disc of the given radius around the start position.

Ion Source tab, gaussian birth distribution: per-axis FWHM; truncation is derived at 3 sigma (L-301) -- an untruncated Gaussian is a different beam, and the derived cut removes the wings without another knob.

The station editor (Ion Source > Stations): a detector or monitor plane at axis = pos with optional windows over the other two axes. `detect` absorbs at first in-window crossing; `record` logs and lets the ion continue. Apply station writes into the live specification and the JSON box.

Voltages.caption: Voltages tab, drive groups: waveform, amplitude, frequency, phase and members are defined once per group; electrodes are assigned below.
Voltages tab, DC ladder groups: feed a chain at both ends and members are interpolated by their explicit number -- order is never parsed from names.
Voltages tab, ladder numbering: auto-number by z orders members by centroid-z straight from the SOLVE masks -- it needs a solved field and refuses rather than guessing.

Physics.caption: Physics tab, Gas sub-tab: the collision model (HS hard-sphere or SDS diffusion), the buffer gas, its pressure and temperature. The dt guidance line underneath is live -- it derives the resolving and collision-sampling limits from the current gas and drive, and warns when the declared step is too coarse for either.

Physics tab, Integration sub-tab: the integration time step and the flight-time ceiling. This is a separate capture because it is a separate sub-tab -- a callout can only box a control the reader can actually see.

Display.caption: Display tab: what the view pane draws and how. The field overlay block at the top drives the shading and its contour lines; the contour slider is the single value authority and the off/on button flips it between 0 and the default of 16.

Impact Analysis.caption: Impact Analysis tab before any flight: the surface dropdown enables once arrivals exist. Stations and enabled boundary faces share one stream and one naming authority (enabled_planes), so the dropdown and the stats table can never disagree.

Geometry Import.caption: Geometry Import tab: bring electrodes in from JSON or STL.

Multi FA.caption: Multi FA tab: staged assemblies -- each stage solves in its own grid and hands the ion across a declared seam.

Config.caption: Config tab: framework version, the examples path, and the example loader. Selecting an example STAGES it and shows its cost BEFORE you commit; Load example applies it.

Status.caption: Status tab after flying Quadrupole (2D, analytic): the run log names the solve, the fly, and the fates.

quickstart.caption: Step 1 -- Config tab: pick Einzel Lens (r-z) in the example loader. Selecting STAGES the example and shows its solve cost before you commit; the Load example button applies it.

Step 2 -- Ion Source tab after loading Einzel Lens (r-z): the deck declares 12 ions on a 3 mm disc at 100 eV along +x, m/z 120. The m/z list is COMMA-DELIMITED: '120' flies one mass; '120, 240' flies a full block of ions at each listed mass.

Step 3 -- check the flight conditions. The Physics tab's Integration sub-tab carries the conditions Einzel Lens (r-z) ships with: a 2 ns time step and a 60 µs flight-time ceiling. Collisions live on the Gas sub-tab beside it and are off for this deck (vacuum). What these fields show is what the integrator receives.

Step 4 -- press Fly: the trajectories draw over the solved geometry in the View pane (the one-button form of the section 2.1 script). xy / xz / yz projections are one click apart, and the 3D Flight Viewer opens the same paths in a rotatable scene.

Step 5 -- the potential-energy landscape the ions flew through: Display tab, shading type 'PE surface (effective)', contour lines at the default 16. For this DC lens the PE surface is the electrostatic potential energy of the ion, so the einzel's three-tube focusing structure reads directly as the shape of the well; the contours off/on button flips the lines with one click.
Step 6 -- the expected result, in the Status tab's run log: the solve, the fly, and the per-fate counts for the 12 ions. This log is the ground truth the chapter-2 prose quotes.

Editor.caption: The geometry editor (/editor), opened on the ion funnel deck: the shape being edited is picked by electrode and index on the left, the perspective scene shows the metal as the solver will rasterize it, and the panel beneath it is the r-x section with the axial coordinate horizontal. Edits are applied to the document, not to a copy: Save writes the deck back to the path shown at the bottom.

The editor's own contour overlay: ticking 'contours' solves the 2-D DC field for the deck on demand and draws the equipotentials over the section, so the effect of moving an electrode is visible in the editor before the deck is ever flown.

Snap-to-pitch and the drag gizmo: with 'snap to pitch' on, a dragged shape lands on the solve lattice rather than between nodes -- the editor's way of keeping metal edges where the rasterizer will actually put them. Undo and Redo step the document's edit history.

3D Flight Viewer.caption: The 3-D Flight Viewer (/flight) on Orbitrap (r-z): the orbits flown in the dashboard, drawn in a rotatable scene with the trap's electrodes. The viewer reads the LAST banked flight -- fly in the dashboard, then press Refresh here. Trajectories are coloured per ion by default; drag to orbit, scroll to zoom, and the perspective is remembered per document across a refresh.

The same Orbitrap (r-z) flight after dragging the camera through roughly a quarter turn. A single projection of a 3-D scene hides an axis: here the second angle is what shows the orbits winding along the wire rather than simply circling it.

examples.caption: Kingdon Trap (r-z): orbital motion around the central wire (0.65 r / 0.76 z rescale verified, L-302).
Kingdon Trap (r-z): hist_traj -- the trajectory-sample histogram of the radius (y in r-z) -- the mode L-302 shipped for orbit dwell structure; the pile-up sits at the radial turning points.
Quadrupole (2D, analytic): stable and ejected masses in one fly -- the analytic rod field shipped by L-302. View pane, xy.
Quadrupole (2D, analytic): Analysis tab, trajectory mode (every recorded point of every ion).
Quadrupole (2D, analytic): Analysis tab, per-ion endpoints.
Quadrupole (2D, analytic): Analysis tab, histogram over per-ion endpoints.
Quadrupole (2D, analytic): Analysis tab, histogram over EVERY recorded sample (hist_traj) of x -- residence-weighted, so where an ion dwells in the confinement plane is where the counts are.

Quadrupole (2D, analytic): the field overlay ON over the same flight -- Display tab, 'shade field / potential' ticked, contour slider at its default of 16. The shading is the instantaneous |E| the ions flew through; the contour lines make the rod quadrupole's saddle structure legible under the trajectories.

Quadrupole (2D, analytic): the contours off/on button after one click -- the shading stays, the lines go, and the slider (the single value authority) now reads 0. A second click restores the default 16; dragging the slider sets any count in between.

Reflectron oa-TOF (2D): orthogonal acceleration, the field-free drift, the ion mirror turnaround and the return to the detector plate, all in one View-pane capture of a real fly (m/z 100 and 500). Electrode labels are turned off here (Display tab checkbox) -- this stack is dense enough that the tags crowd the beam; your own session shows them by default.

Reflectron oa-TOF (2D): Impact Analysis at the DETECTOR station declared on the plate face (y = 32.0 mm, windowed to the 21-35 mm plate span). The impact-xy cross-section shows where the packet lands across the plate (this deck is planar, so z is identically zero); the signal-vs-t histogram of the same arrivals is the mass spectrum -- two masses, two peaks.
